chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān:

O Allah, place light in my heart, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight, and in my flesh, my blood, my bones, my veins, my joints, my sitting place, my standing place, my entrance, and my exit, light; and magnify light for me, O Lord, on the day I meet You.
Indeed, You are powerful over all things.

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: A direct invocation meaning 'O Allah,' opening the supplication.
key_terms.بَصَرِي: My sight; the faculty of seeing, both physically and spiritually.
key_terms.سَمْعِي: My hearing; the faculty of receiving and responding to guidance.
key_terms.قَدِيرٌ: All-powerful; describing Allah's complete power over all things.
key_terms.قَلْبِي: My heart; the inner faculty for faith, perception, and spiritual awareness.
key_terms.نُورًا: Light; divine illumination sought for the heart, senses, body, and circumstances.
key_terms.يَوْمَ أَلْقَاكَ: The day I meet You; a reference to the Hereafter and standing before Allah.

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asking Allah to place light in every part of a person?
ai.summary: This hadith records a du'a asking Allah to fill the supplicant's inner and outer being with light in every faculty and state. It concludes by invoking Allah's absolute power and by seeking divine light especially for the day of لقاء with Him, linking worship in this world to the Hereafter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3136 - In the narration of Abdullah ibn Sinan:

"O Allah (swt), place light in my heart, light in my hearing, light in my sight, light in my flesh, light in my blood, light in my bones, light in my veins, light in my joints, light in my sitting place, light in my standing place, light in my entrance, and light in my exit. O Lord (azj), magnify light for me on the day I meet You.
Indeed, You are capable of all things."
